References / Illustration / 478

Jack Smith and Jeremy Rieger, “Lotus” artwork

A square artwork in gray and violet: a melted-chrome flower in an arched frame, a tall liquid display word, op-art spirals, and Japanese katakana.

Source
AIGA Eye on Design (5 September 2019): “Acid Graphics” Are the New Psychedelia
Creator
Jack Smith and Jeremy Rieger
Made
Not stated (before September 2019)
Style
Acid graphics (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Eerie, psychedelic, dense
Evidence
Inspected the 1200 px image Lotus-By-Jack-Smith-and-Jeremy-Rieger.jpg that Eye on Design published with the article, in a scratch folder. Not stored. The object is a digital image as the magazine published it, not a named physical copy. The caption reads “Lotus by Jack Smith and Jeremy Rieger, as featured on @acidgraphix”.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Eye on Design shows the work in its 2019 article on acid graphics, with the caption “Lotus by Jack Smith and Jeremy Rieger, as featured on @acidgraphix”.

Observed

  • The ground is black with scratches and dust, like a worn sleeve.
  • A flower in an arched frame is rendered as melted, reflective gray chrome with hard black contours.
  • A tall word runs down the left in melted, wavy pale-gray letters, with violet ivy growing over it. Katakana run down the right and across the lower left.
  • Violet concentric rings form a long capsule at the top. Black-and-white op-art spirals and violet dots run down the right edge.
  • Small pseudo-script text sits in violet at the lower right.

Why it belongs

The work has the liquid-chrome surface, the melted lettering, and the op-art patterns of the style in a dense layout. Its violet accent shows that acid green is common but not required.

Borrow

Put a liquid-chrome image in an arched frame and surround it with op-art spirals.

Draw one display word as melted, wavy letters and let a plant motif grow over it.
